fr-0HXZ.title: Location: island east of Madagascar
fr-0HXZ.summary: An overseas department east of Madagascar. It counts as France for country streaks.

differs.how: Madagascar is a separate country

fr-1rIs.title: Google car: coloured flags on antenna
fr-1rIs.summary: Rarely, the Gen 3 antenna has a flag. All the coloured flags are unique here, and learning where each appears can score a lot.

fr-2v01.title: Language: Basque, K X Z, thin font
fr-2v01.summary: Basque signs are in the western half of the Pyrenees department next to Spanish Basque country. Common letters are K, X and Z, and direction signs use a thinner font. Street is karrika, not Spain's kalea.

differs.how: Spanish Basque country uses 'kalea' for street

fr-3Q5x.title: Postal codes: first two digits are the department
fr-3Q5x.summary: Postal codes have 5 digits, the first two being the department number, mostly alphabetical. The same numbers appear in the blue strip on plates.

fr-4OYB.title: Sign: town entry with red border, thin white outline
fr-4OYB.summary: Town entry signs have a red border with a thin white outline.

fr-4kQ6.title: Plate: long white, blue strip each side
fr-4kQ6.summary: Long white plates with a blue strip on both sides, the left more visible. Old rear plates can be yellow and lack the right strip, but are rare. Italy has two equal blue strips and shorter front plates.

differs.how: two equally visible blue strips, shorter front plate

fr-4ocl.title: Street sign: city name on street signs
fr-4ocl.summary: Street signs around Paris often show the city name, which is unusual elsewhere. They are often modern, and many names relate to the Seine or Marne. It also appears sporadically elsewhere.

fr-6TPW.title: Route marker: D-road with decimal number
fr-6TPW.summary: In that same department D-roads with a superscript number are most common. On the map they show as decimals, like D134.10. Rare elsewhere.

fr-7CKN.title: Roofs: steep black mansard with dormer windows
fr-7CKN.summary: Steep black shingle mansard roofs with dormer windows are very common in the capital. Not unique, but a good clue in large numbers and on wide boulevards.

fr-7oyS.title: Language: Celtic, d k w and ñ
fr-7oyS.summary: Breton is Celtic and looks like Welsh, with letters d, k, w and ñ. It appears on bilingual signs across Brittany, as far east as Rennes, rarely Nantes. Its word for street is straed.

differs.how: looks like Welsh, but uses ñ

fr-8uNz.title: Houses: white walls, coloured timber frames
fr-8uNz.summary: White houses with often colourful timber framing, matching shutters and gates, are typical of the Basque area and beyond. Northern Spain has them too, but with unpainted timber.

differs.how: timber frames are usually unpainted

fr-944S.title: Language: accents é à è â ê î ô ç and œ
fr-944S.summary: A Romance language with accents (é, è, à, â, ê, î, ô, û), tréma (ë, ï, ü), ç and œ. Words ending in -ux are only French. Belgium, Luxembourg, Monaco and Switzerland also speak it.

fr-A0j5.title: Flag: red and yellow horizontal stripes
fr-A0j5.summary: A flag of red and yellow horizontal stripes is the flag and department logo of the far-south Pyrenees department, often shown in coats of arms on street signs. Provence's flag is similar but vertical.

fr-AUP3.title: Plants: sunflowers
fr-AUP3.summary: Sunflowers are mostly in the southwest, especially around Toulouse.

fr-AUpF.title: Town names: common endings by region
fr-AUpF.summary: Place name endings are crucial for guessing the region. The map shows the most common ones, with a few exceptions.

fr-AXar.title: Language: Occitan, carrer-like street word
fr-AXar.summary: Occitan is close to Catalan, spread thinly in the south, mostly on city street signs. Street words like 'carrièra' (southwest) and 'carriero' (southeast coast) resemble Catalan 'carrer'.

fr-AuxP.title: Sign: small yellow road number plate, D-road
fr-AuxP.summary: Small yellow signs with the road number, usually starting with D, often on top of direction or town entry signs. Only found here.

fr-Bn7U.title: Pole: arrowhead top, insulators on top
fr-Bn7U.summary: Some pole tops have the insulators on top and look like an arrowhead. Only found here.

fr-BzxF.title: Houses: timber frames, half-hip, fish-scale tiles
fr-BzxF.summary: German-style elements in the east: timber framing, half-hip roofs and fish-scale tiles. They appear elsewhere sometimes, so look for several together.

fr-CIlO.title: Street sign: red slanted fleur-de-lis
fr-CIlO.summary: Street signs with a red slanted fleur-de-lis are unique to Lille.

fr-CNdg.title: Sign: pedestrian sign with 5 stripes, split head
fr-CNdg.summary: Pedestrian crossing sign with five stripes and a head detached from the body, with the usual wide white border. Less commonly two dashed lines instead of stripes.

fr-CuZO.title: Sign: azure blue signposts
fr-CuZO.summary: On the Riviera, regular traffic signposts are painted azure blue, and one town west of Nice has lighter powder blue ones. Blue infrastructure appears elsewhere, especially Brittany, so check the landscape.

fr-DCU8.title: Pole: concrete with step-like indents
fr-DCU8.summary: Concrete poles with step-like indents, called ladder or waffle poles. Common in Spain too.

fr-Ducm.title: Road: reddish-purple tinted asphalt
fr-Ducm.summary: Roads with a clear red, purple or burgundy tint are mostly between Paris and Dijon, except Normandy. Normal roads can look reddish in some light, so be careful.

fr-DwIX.title: Plants: lavender fields
fr-DwIX.summary: Lavender fields grow in the southeast and look like small grey bushes when young.

fr-EDtV.title: Roofs: black shingles in the northwest
fr-EDtV.summary: Black shingle roofs are mainly in the northwest, cut off roughly at the Loire. Also near the Belgian border, south-centre and Pyrenees, so black roofs help in Alps vs Pyrenees choices.

fr-Eqaj.title: Guardrail: A-type, usually no reflectors
fr-Eqaj.summary: Mostly A-type guardrails without reflectors. Thin B-type, the standard in Czechia and Slovakia, appears rarely. Spanish, Andorran and Belgian guardrails have yellow reflectors.

differs.how: yellow reflectors on guardrails
yellow reflectors on guardrails

fr-F1Hp.title: Walls: cuboid stone and mortar barriers
fr-F1Hp.summary: Cuboid stone-and-mortar barriers are common on Corsica. Not unique, but think of the island when you see them in Mediterranean land. Rounded-top stone barriers are not found there.

fr-HNgr.title: Roofs: overlapping rounded tiles in the south
fr-HNgr.summary: Roofs in the south are often made of overlapping rounded tiles, often in varied colours.

fr-IaD0.title: Route marker: yellow or red semicircle on white
fr-IaD0.summary: Km markers usually have a yellow or red semicircle on top of a white rectangle, as a waystone or flat sign, parallel or perpendicular to the road. Big highways have square markers with a red top.

fr-Izqw.title: Location: eastern Caribbean island
fr-Izqw.summary: An overseas department in the eastern Caribbean. It counts as France for streaks.

fr-KFEi.title: Houses: Breton houses with colourful fronts
fr-KFEi.summary: On one Breton island, local-style houses have colourful façades and outlines, a bit like Portugal. The island has only oversaturated Gen 2 coverage.

differs.how: similar colourful houses, but Gen 2 camera here

fr-L753.title: Guardrail: thin B-type on northern highways
fr-L753.summary: Thin B-type guardrail, standard in Czechia and Slovakia, is sometimes found on northern highways from Le Mans, Tours, Paris, Reims and Metz. Often a minority there, and more common but less reliable on small northern roads.

differs.how: Czech Republic uses thin B-type as standard
Slovakia uses thin B-type as standard

fr-LYka.title: Language: Catalan, word 'carrer'
fr-LYka.summary: The far southern department uses Catalan, close to Spanish and French, with more Ç than French. Street is 'carrer'.

fr-MGk9.title: Street sign: small 'Arr' plate in a non-split city
fr-MGk9.summary: Small tables saying 'Arrᵗ' on a separate sign are found in Bordeaux, even though it has no arrondissements.

fr-NnH1.title: Sign: dark green post, light green back
fr-NnH1.summary: In the northern department of Pas-de-Calais, a dark green post with a lighter green back (matcha to turquoise), sometimes with a green and blue triangle logo. In some light it looks like the greyish signs.

fr-NqvK.title: Sign: white direction sign, offset black outline
fr-NqvK.summary: White direction signs with a black outline slightly in from the edge, arrow-shaped with a thicker border at the point. Highways are blue or green. Small places are often in italics.

fr-NqvL.title: Bollard: round white with two indented bands
fr-NqvL.summary: A round white post with two reflective indented bands. Also in green or yellow versions. Only found here.

fr-NtOc.title: Sign: very short signposts
fr-NtOc.summary: Traffic signs on particularly short posts are very common.

fr-OE0N.title: Language: German-like signs, gasse or strasse
fr-OE0N.summary: Alsatian, a German dialect, shows on bilingual signs in the east using gasse or strasse. Streets with German names are also concentrated there.

fr-P6Wi.title: Bollard: wedge shape, wide white reflectors
fr-P6Wi.summary: A wedge-shaped bollard with wide rectangular white reflectors on front and back. Less common, and only found here.

fr-RaDU.title: Road lines: unusually long centre dashes
fr-RaDU.summary: Unusually long centre dashes are a good clue. The UK has long dashes too.

differs.how: also has very long centre dashes

fr-RkYB.title: Phone numbers: 10 digits, 01 to 05 by region
fr-RkYB.summary: Ten digits starting with a regional code: 01 is the Paris area, 02 to 05 go clockwise from the northwest. Numbers starting 06 to 09 are not regional.

fr-SEfx.title: Houses: cream and orange stone, red brick details
fr-SEfx.summary: Uneven cream-to-orange stone walls with mortar and red brick details are in the towns around Paris, but usually not in Paris itself.

fr-TAw8.title: Road lines: end-of-passing-zone arrows
fr-TAw8.summary: Arrows on the road at the end of a passing zone, with the centre dashes very close together. Spain, Portugal and Romania have them too. In the UK they point to the left lane.

differs.how: arrows point to the left lane

fr-VVMi.title: Plants: stone pines along the south coast
fr-VVMi.summary: Stone pines grow along the south coast, often planted along city roads. They can be found as far north as Nantes.

fr-VYms.title: Towns: names starting with Plou-
fr-VYms.summary: Towns whose names start with Plou- are in the northwest of Brittany.

fr-WVZz.title: Houses: light base, lots of wood
fr-WVZz.summary: Alpine houses have a light base and lots of wood. Similar houses exist in tourist parts of the Pyrenees.

fr-WdcG.title: Cars: Peugeot, Renault, Citroën
fr-WdcG.summary: Peugeot, Renault and Citroën make up almost half of all cars. Neighbouring French-speaking countries have them too.

fr-Wop3.title: Sign: burgundy red parts on direction signs
fr-Wop3.summary: Direction signs in one southwestern department often have burgundy red fittings and ornaments, sometimes with yellow signposts.

fr-XTPv.title: Language: six minority languages
fr-XTPv.summary: Six minority languages: Alsatian, Basque, Breton, Catalan, Corsican and Occitan. French dominates everywhere, so don't rule out regions in all-French rounds.

fr-Xe70.title: Plants: pure maritime pine forests, flat
fr-Xe70.summary: Forests made entirely of maritime pines are in the southwest (Gironde and Landes), on very flat land, unlike other pine areas.

fr-YfZM.title: Landscape: salt farms along the Atlantic coast
fr-YfZM.summary: Salt farms look like flooded trenches with grass strips between them. Found along the Atlantic coast, notably Guérande, Noirmoutier, Île de Ré and Île d'Oléron.

fr-ZUqh.title: Street sign: green and Prussian blue with arch
fr-ZUqh.summary: Paris uses an iconic green and Prussian blue sign with an arched top, copied in Bucharest. The plain rectangle appears in nearby towns and rarely elsewhere.

differs.how: Bucharest copies the Paris sign; check language

fr-aay7.title: Street sign: 'Arr' district on the big three
fr-aay7.summary: Paris, Lyon and Marseille are the only cities split into arrondissements (shown as Arrᵗ or Arrt.). The district shows on the map, which helps pinpoint.

fr-aoTH.title: Houses: dark red brick rows near Belgium
fr-aoTH.summary: Rows of dark red brick houses, like Flemish ones in Belgium, are near the Belgian border. Bricks may be outlined with white mortar.

differs.how: similar bricks, use plates and language

fr-b14O.title: Sign: red border with thin white outline
fr-b14O.summary: Road signs have a red border with a thin white outline, and often a white rectangular sign with black text below. Spain's red border is thick and goes to the edge.

differs.how: thick red border going all the way to the edge

fr-cqw6.title: Town names: -sur-river, -sur-mer, -plage
fr-cqw6.summary: Many cities carry their river name, like Chalonnes-sur-Loire (sur is often shortened). Names with -sur-mer or -plage are only on the coast.

fr-d3xx.title: Sign: wine-red square signposts
fr-d3xx.summary: On the edge of Bordeaux, square traffic signposts are in wine red. Red posts alone are not unique, so use with caution.

fr-drHI.title: Sign: town entry and exit in one thick block
fr-drHI.summary: Town entry signs in one northeastern department combine entry and exit into one noticeably thicker block.

fr-eNYi.title: Bollard: round white, pointed top, reflector band
fr-eNYi.summary: A round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band all the way around, grey or red. Rare ones have a fully red top. Scottish bollards look similar but have a blunt top.

differs.how: Scottish version has a blunt top, not pointed

fr-eWQD.title: Houses: Brittany style, black roofs, edge chimneys
fr-eWQD.summary: A very consistent style: black roofs, chimneys on the gable edge, black slate walls and stone around doors and windows. Walls are very light or stone.

fr-etqG.title: Regions: 13 regions and 96 departments
fr-etqG.summary: The guide uses 13 regions and 96 departments. Departments are named after geographic features and their logos appear on infrastructure.

fr-gORW.title: Chevron: white arrows on blue, one to five
fr-gORW.summary: Chevrons with white arrows on blue, with one to five arrows. Spain has this colour scheme too, but only with two or four arrows.

differs.how: only two or four arrows

fr-iaMC.title: Pole: diamond top with three wires
fr-iaMC.summary: A diamond-shaped pole top with three wires, mostly on top of ladder poles. Spain has this combination too.

fr-jPuX.title: Plants: vineyards
fr-jPuX.summary: France is the second biggest wine producer. Main areas: around Bordeaux, the south coast and Champagne east of Paris. Others: Loire Valley, Alsace and Corsica.

fr-jkin.title: Sign: brown post and brown back
fr-jkin.summary: Signs where both post and back are brown are most common east of Paris (Seine-et-Marne), rarely in Brittany. More reliable with square posts, but round ones are as common.

fr-k4sk.title: Flag: red and yellow with a cross, stripes
fr-k4sk.summary: A red and yellow logo with a cross and vertical stripes is the flag of the southern region of Occitanie. Other regions have logos that appear less often.

fr-kpiu.title: Houses: bright orange brick, shutters
fr-kpiu.summary: In old towns around Toulouse you often see bright orange brick buildings, brighter than the northern ones, with Mediterranean touches like wooden shutters.

fr-l4nF.title: Houses: palms, light multi-storey buildings, balconies
fr-l4nF.summary: The Riviera looks like Monaco: wealthy areas with planted palms and light multi-storey buildings with wide balconies. Other southern coast towns feel similar. Several harbours have boat trekkers.

differs.how: looks the same, use plates and signs

fr-lVS8.title: Logos: each department has its own
fr-lVS8.summary: Most departments have their own logo, often with initials or the full name, on bus stops, km markers, trail banners, direction signs and signbacks. Useful to know what they stand for, but not for beginners.

fr-lm-303251.title: Google car: blue flag on antenna
fr-lm-303251.summary: A blue flag on the Gen 3 antenna is found in Bas-Rhin, Aube and the Corrèze, Haute-Vienne and Dordogne area.

fr-lm-303252.title: Language: street word 'carrièra'
fr-lm-303252.summary: 'Carrièra', the Occitan word for street, is found in south-central France.

fr-lm-303253.title: Language: street word 'carriero'
fr-lm-303253.summary: 'Carriero', the Provençal word for street, is found on the south-east coast.

fr-lm-303254.title: Google car: black and white flag on antenna
fr-lm-303254.summary: A black and white flag on the Gen 3 antenna is found in Calvados, Orne, eastern Bourgogne and the Loire and Haute-Loire area.

fr-lm-303255.title: Google car: red flag on antenna
fr-lm-303255.summary: A red flag on the Gen 3 antenna is only in the eastern part of the Nord department.

fr-lm-303256.title: Town name ending: -ac
fr-lm-303256.summary: Place names ending in -ac are found in the southwest and in Brittany.

fr-lm-303257.title: Town name ending: -as
fr-lm-303257.summary: Place names ending in -as are found in the southern half.

fr-lm-303258.title: Town name ending: -at
fr-lm-303258.summary: Place names ending in -at are found in the central south.

fr-lm-303259.title: Town name ending: -ay
fr-lm-303259.summary: Place names ending in -ay are found in the northern half.

fr-lm-303260.title: Town name ending: -ville
fr-lm-303260.summary: Place names ending in -ville are found in the northeast and Normandy, and sometimes between.

fr-lm-303261.title: Town name ending: -ey
fr-lm-303261.summary: Place names ending in -ey are found on the eastern border, in Normandy and in the southwest.

fr-lm-303262.title: Town name ending: -court
fr-lm-303262.summary: Place names ending in -court are found in the north and northeast.

fr-lm-303263.title: Town name ending: -ach
fr-lm-303263.summary: Place names ending in -ach are found in Alsace.

fr-lm-303264.title: Town name ending: -heim
fr-lm-303264.summary: Place names ending in -heim are found in Alsace.

fr-lm-303265.title: Town name ending: -iller
fr-lm-303265.summary: Place names ending in -iller are found in Alsace.

fr-lm-303266.title: Town name ending: -caux
fr-lm-303266.summary: Place names ending in -caux are found in Seine-Maritime.

fr-lm-303267.title: Town name ending: -brie
fr-lm-303267.summary: Place names ending in -brie are found in Seine-et-Marne.

fr-lm-303268.title: Town name ending: -beauce
fr-lm-303268.summary: Place names ending in -beauce are found between Essonne and Vendôme.

fr-lm-303269.title: Town name ending: -anjou
fr-lm-303269.summary: Place names ending in -anjou are found in Maine-et-Loire.

fr-lm-303270.title: Town name ending: -touraine
fr-lm-303270.summary: Place names ending in -touraine are found in Indre-et-Loire.

fr-lm-303271.title: Town name ending: -bearn
fr-lm-303271.summary: Place names ending in -bearn are found in Pyrénées-Atlantiques.

fr-lm-303272.title: Town name ending: -quercy
fr-lm-303272.summary: Place names ending in -quercy are found in Lot and Tarn-et-Garonne.

fr-lm-303273.title: Town name ending: -bresse
fr-lm-303273.summary: Place names ending in -bresse are found on the border between Jura and Saône-et-Loire.

fr-lm-473878.title: Pole: spiked top on wooden poles
fr-lm-473878.summary: Hard to tell from Ireland and the UK? Look at the tops of the wooden poles: here they have a spiked top.

differs.how: no spiked pole tops
no spiked pole tops

fr-lm-498443.title: Houses: low, white walls, red roofs on the west coast
fr-lm-498443.summary: Houses along the west coast from Nantes to Bayonne are usually low, with white walls and red roofs.

fr-lm-498446.title: Plate: yellow front plates near Luxembourg
fr-lm-498446.summary: Old coverage can show yellow rear plates. Several yellow front plates suggest you are near Luxembourg.

differs.how: yellow front plates are normal there

fr-lm-507804.title: Plants: corn fields in the west
fr-lm-507804.summary: Corn fields are mostly in the west, plus some areas east of Paris and around Lyon and Strasbourg.

fr-lm-507805.title: Landscape: very flat industrial fields, no hedges
fr-lm-507805.summary: The Beauce region south of Paris is one of the flattest, with industrial-size fields of potatoes or cereals and no hedges, unlike the west.

fr-lm-507806.title: Animals: cows, horses and sheep
fr-lm-507806.summary: Livestock is most often seen in the west (Brittany, Normandy) and in the mountains (Pyrenees, Alps).

fr-lm-558155.title: Street sign: special corners with dots
fr-lm-558155.summary: Nantes and Rennes share this street sign with special corners and dots. Nantes is much bigger, so guess it unless you know it's Rennes.

fr-lm-837.title: Language: useful words
fr-lm-837.summary: Handy words: bois woods, plage beach, la poste post office, toutes directions all directions, centre ville city centre, pont bridge, école school, à louer for rent.

fr-mVDK.title: Sign: red-white-red tall rectangles on sticks
fr-mVDK.summary: Roadsides may have tall rectangles on sticks in the colours of the Austrian flag, found nowhere else.

fr-mcDH.title: Street sign: four corner bolts, notched white border
fr-mcDH.summary: Lyon's signs have four corner bolts and an unbroken inner white border with notches for the district and each bolt. Outside Lyon proper the suburb name is shown.

fr-n2Xh.title: Google car: low-mounted camera, big round blur
fr-n2Xh.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a fairly big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through. Most of Western Europe has it.

fr-nPXX.title: Plants: tall hedges blocking the view
fr-nPXX.summary: Rural roads with hedges blocking the view, like the British Isles, are mainly in the northwest, especially Normandy. Hedges alone are common everywhere.

fr-o8dK.title: Street sign: city emblem, Greek-style cross
fr-o8dK.summary: Marseille's street signs usually carry the city emblem, a variation of the Greek cross, and the white border is broken at the top even if the cross is missing.

fr-pP2z.title: Houses: stone, pastel, gable roofs, orange tiles
fr-pP2z.summary: Mostly stone houses, unpainted or in grey or yellow pastels, with simple gable roofs of orange tiles or sometimes black slate. Townhouses often touch along the road. Regional styles vary a lot.

fr-perh.title: Language: street is 'rue'
fr-perh.summary: The word for street is 'rue'. Belgium uses it on street signs too.

fr-pf4x.title: Road lines: centre dashes of two offset blocks
fr-pf4x.summary: Centre lines where each dash is two offset blocks. Not very common, but a sure sign of the country.

fr-rDFi.title: Language: Italian-like words ending in u
fr-rDFi.summary: On Corsica you find signs in Corsican, close to Italian, with words ending in vowels and endings -u, -iu, -ju. Place names often have Italian origins.

fr-rGE0.title: Sign: dark green signposts and backs
fr-rGE0.summary: Dark green signposts and backs are most common in Brittany and around Paris, plus several southern regions. They can appear elsewhere.

fr-rdKk.title: House number: blue serif plates
fr-rdKk.summary: House numbers are most often blue in a serif font with slightly exaggerated shapes. Italy almost never uses blue house numbers.

differs.how: almost never uses blue house numbers

fr-s0La.title: Pole: small blue plate
fr-s0La.summary: Small blue rectangular plates on utility poles, found only here. On almost all wooden and metal poles, less often on ladder poles.

fr-u1uQ.title: Pole: wood or thin octagonal metal
fr-u1uQ.summary: Wooden poles and thin octagonal metal poles are very common in the countryside and small towns.

fr-umtN.title: Street sign: blue M on white, top left
fr-umtN.summary: Street signs with a blue 'M' on a white background in the top left corner mean Montpellier.

fr-vSP7.title: Road lines: long spaced-out edge dashes
fr-vSP7.summary: Typical roads have long dashes with big gaps on the outside edge.

fr-wDHB.title: Location: islands south of Newfoundland
fr-wDHB.summary: A self-governing territory of France south of Newfoundland in Canada. It counts as France for streaks.

differs.how: Canada is a separate country

fr-xk28.title: Landscape: high southeast, flat north
fr-xk28.summary: The tallest mountains are in the southeast and along the Spanish border. The north and west coast are flat or rolling, and the south is hillier.

fr-xp6R.title: Sign: green sticker on dark green back
fr-xp6R.summary: In one department near Paris, signbacks may carry the green department logo, usually on a dark green back with a mismatched post.

fr-xsxc.title: Landmark: wind turbines in the north
fr-xsxc.summary: Wind turbines are far more common in the north.

fr-yTq3.title: Sign: flat rectangular signposts
fr-yTq3.summary: Many traffic signs sit on flat rectangular posts, and posts or backs may be oddly coloured. Only Portugal, Spain and Andorra also use flat posts in Europe.

fr-zDEN.title: Sign: greyish green back on darker green post
fr-zDEN.summary: A greyish green signback on a darker green post is found in three areas: Brittany (north coast and east), the southwest corner, and rarely near the Alps.
